lockup.summary: The company, its directors, officers and holders of nearly all its stock agreed not to sell for 180 days after the prospectus date without written consent from J.P. Morgan and Evercore.

what: TRex Bio is a drug company testing medicines that use immune cells in body tissue to treat autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about $103.5 million. About $90.0 million is for Phase 2 trials of TRB-061 and about $10.0 million for a Phase 1 trial of TRB-071. The rest is for general business needs.
risks: The company is young, has no approved products and has lost money in every year except one, and it expects more losses.
Raising more money later may dilute current shareholders, limit how the company operates, or force it to give up rights to its drug candidates.
The company depends heavily on two drug candidates, TRB-061 and TRB-071, and their clinical trials may not succeed.
Trouble enrolling and treating patients in clinical trials could delay the trials or block the approvals the company needs.
Serious side effects from its drug candidates could delay or stop approval or market acceptance, or cause problems after approval.
